mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has stabilized near zero over the past four weeks (t-3w: -1.6, t-0w: +0.3), indicating a floor effect. Continued stability in WORKPLACES (3.9 to 4.7 range) and TRANSIT (near +0.6) sustains commuting patterns that generate incidental retail visits, driving RETAIL_REC positive over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days falls below or equals the mean of the last 28 days, or WORKPLACES drops below 2.0 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated GROCERY_PHARM mobility (42.9–44.4 range) reflects sustained essential-goods purchasing behavior. This high baseline in essential trips creates habit-stacking conditions where consumers combine grocery visits with retail-and-recreation stops, generating a +0.5 to +1.5 percentage-point lift in RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 42.0 for all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or remains flat over the next 28 days despite GROCERY_PHARM staying above 42.0, or GROCERY_PHARM falls below 40.0 in any week.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-November in Singapore marks the onset of year-end holiday shopping season. PARKS mobility remains suppressed (−6.7), indicating outdoor recreation is not the primary draw. Instead, consumers redirect discretionary time toward indoor retail-and-recreation venues, producing a +2.0 to +3.5 percentage-point increase in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks independent of other mobility signals.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days relative to the last 28 days, or PARKS rises above −3.0 and RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility are coupled (both near +0.6 in recent weeks), indicating stable commuting. When both remain above +0.5 simultaneously, they sustain a critical mass of weekday foot traffic that anchors retail-and-recreation visits. A joint decline in either series below +0.3 for two consecutive weeks would break this anchor and suppress RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain above +0.3 for the next two weeks
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT falls below +0.3 for two consecutive weeks in the forecast period, or RETAIL_REC declines despite both proxies remaining above +0.3.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from +4.0 (t-3w) to +3.7 (t-0w), signaling a gradual return to pre-pandemic baseline patterns. This normalization of home-time suggests restrictions are easing or compliance is weakening. If RESIDENTIAL continues declining toward +2.0 over the next two weeks, consumers will reallocate time to retail-and-recreation venues, producing a +1.0 to +2.0 percentage-point lift.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines by more than 0.2 percentage points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL stabilizes or increases over the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not rise despite RESIDENTIAL declining as specified.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS mobility show inverse patterns (GROCERY_PHARM +42.9, PARKS −6.7). High grocery traffic combined with suppressed outdoor recreation indicates consumers are consolidating trips to indoor venues. This trip-consolidation behavior extends to retail-and-recreation, where grocery-adjacent retail (malls, shopping centers) capture incremental visits, driving RETAIL_REC up by +1.5 to +2.5 percentage points over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM above 42.0 AND PARKS below −5.0 simultaneously
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days, or either GROCERY_PHARM falls below 41.0 or PARKS rises above −4.0 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has been stable at +0.6 for three consecutive weeks (t-2w, t-1w, t-0w), indicating robust public-transport usage. This sustained transit signal is a leading indicator of retail-and-recreation demand, as transit users are more likely to visit retail venues during commute-adjacent time windows. A one-week horizon mechanism predicts RETAIL_REC will rise by +0.3 to +0.8 percentage points in the immediate week following sustained TRANSIT stability.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains above +0.5 for the current week
failure_condition: TRANSIT falls below +0.3 in the next week, or RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week following sustained TRANSIT above +0.5.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility (4.3 in t-0w) and RESIDENTIAL mobility (3.7 in t-0w) show a widening gap (0.6 percentage points), indicating workers are spending more time at workplaces relative to home. This shift in time allocation, combined with stable TRANSIT (+0.6), creates a three-way interaction where commuting workers have both the means (transit) and the opportunity (time away from home) to visit retail venues. Over four weeks, this interaction produces a +1.5 to +2.5 percentage-point increase in RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES exceeds RESIDENTIAL by more than 0.5 percentage points for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: The gap between WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL narrows below 0.3 percentage points, or RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days despite the specified gap condition being met.
